title: PYSEC-2025-19
summary: Affected: PyPI: picklescan picklescan before 0.0.22 only considers standard pickle file extensions in the scope for its vulnerability scan. An attacker could craft a malicious model that uses Pickle and include a malicious pickle file with a non-standard file extension. Because the malicious pickle file inclusion is not considered as part of the scope of picklescan, the file would pass security checks and appear to be safe, when it could instead prove to be problematic.

title: PYSEC-2024-115
summary: Affected: PyPI: langchain-community A vulnerability in the GraphCypherQAChain class of langchain-ai/langchain-community version 0.2.5 allows for SQL injection through prompt injection. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data manipulation, data exfiltration, denial of service (DoS) by deleting all data, breaches in multi-tenant security environments, and data integrity issues. Attackers can create, update, or delete nodes and relationships without proper authorization, extract sensitive data, disrupt services, access data across different tenants, and compromise the integrity of the database.

title: GHSA-pqh8-p93p-2rx7 — @dynatrace-oss/dynatrace-mcp-server has a DQL injection via parameters not documented as DQL
summary:
Affected: npm: @dynatrace-oss/dynatrace-mcp-server ### Summary
A DQL injection vulnerability in several read tools lets a caller bypass the tools' documented field-scope, time-window, and display caps by injecting DQL pipeline stages through parameters typed as identifiers. ### Details
Several tools interpolate caller-supplied parameters directly into DQL query strings without quoting or escaping. The affected parameters are documented in their Zod schemas as identifiers or constrained shorthand (such as `"24h"` timeframe values or Kubernetes UIDs) - not as DQL expressions. The interpolation lets a caller break out of string literals, append arbitrary DQL pipeline stages, and use `//` line comments (documented in the [Dynatrace DQL language reference](https://docs.dynatrace.com/docs/discover-dynatrace/platform/grail/dynatrace-query-language/dql-reference)) to discard the rest of the intended query. The marginal-privilege ceiling is low because the operator's token also exposes `execute_dql` with full DQL access. What the injection grants is the ability to bypass the affected tools' contract: the `readOnlyHint: true` annotation that MCP clients may treat as a signal to auto-approve, the per-tool field selection (e.g., `| fields id, name, type`), the display caps (`maxProblemsToDisplay`, `maxVulnerabilitiesToDisplay`, `maxEntitiesToDisplay`), and the time-window bounds. title: GHSA-8cfq-jgf7-8m27 — traQ: Privilege escalation by OAuth prompt=none request
summary:
Affected: Go: github.com/traPtitech/traQ In OAuth2 silent authorization (`prompt=none`), when the `scope` parameter was empty or omitted, all scopes registered for the OAuth client became eligible for issuance. However, the prior consent check was performed against the empty requested scope set. As a result, an attacker could obtain an access token with broader scopes than the user had previously consented to, without requiring additional consent. ## Impact If an attacker controls an OAuth client capable of receiving authorization codes, and a user has already consented to only a subset of that client’s scopes, the attacker may be able to obtain a token containing all scopes registered for that client by sending an authorization request with `prompt=none` and an empty or omitted `scope`. If the user has not consented to the client at all, `consent_required` is returned as usual. ## Patches This issue has been fixed in v3.28.3. After the fix, the consent check for `prompt=none` verifies the scopes that will actually be issued, rather than the empty requested scope set. If the user has not consented to all scopes after expansion, `consent_required` is returned. traQ also recommends revoking any existing OAuth tokens created before the fix if they were potentially affected. ## Workarounds If users cannot update immediately, they should apply the following mitigations: - Disable untrusted OAuth clients, minimize registered client scopes, and revoke existing tokens

title: GHSA-xrmj-5g4g-8987 — @dynatrace-oss/dynatrace-mcp-server has a workflow template injection via create_workflow_for_notification
summary:
Affected: npm: @dynatrace-oss/dynatrace-mcp-server ### Summary
A template injection vulnerability in the `create_workflow_for_notification` tool lets a caller embed Jinja2 expressions that the Dynatrace workflow engine evaluates at runtime, exfiltrating event data to attacker-controlled destinations through a workflow that persists in the tenant after the MCP session ends. ### Details
The `create_workflow_for_notification` tool interpolates three caller-supplied parameters (`teamName`, `problemType`, `channel`) directly into a Dynatrace Workflow definition. Dynatrace Workflows use Jinja2 templating: per the [official documentation](https://docs.dynatrace.com/docs/analyze-explore-automate/workflows/reference), `{{ ... }}` expressions in action inputs are evaluated at workflow runtime for every action except `Run Javascript` (which is carved out specifically to avoid code injection). A caller can therefore supply, for example, `teamName = "{{ event() }}"` and have the workflow engine evaluate that expression at runtime, serialising the full event object into the message body delivered to the Slack channel. title: GHSA-p74g-f95m-7fx7 — traQ: XSS in the User Uploaded File Retrieval API
summary:
Affected: Go: github.com/traPtitech/traQ ### Impact For instances where `TRAQ_STORAGE_TYPE` is set to `local`, the file retrieval API `/files/{fileId}` could serve user-uploaded SVG or HTML files in a way that allowed them to be rendered directly in the browser. As a result, an attacker who can upload files to traQ could upload a crafted SVG or HTML file and trick a victim into opening the file URL, allowing the attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser. ### Patches This issue has been fixed in v3.28.3. After this fix, the file retrieval API always adds the `Content-Disposition` header to its responses regardless of the value of the `dl` query parameter. This prevents user-uploaded files from being displayed directly in the browser. ### Workarounds To mitigate the impact of this issue, apply either of the following workarounds: * Change `TRAQ_STORAGE_TYPE` to a storage backend other than `local`.
* Ensure that all requests to `/files/{fileId}` include `dl=1`. Users of this application can reduce the risk of exploitation by avoiding suspicious file URLs.

title: GHSA-4xm8-rg9h-jhq2 — Signal K resources API path traversal can disclose the JWT signing secret and enable remote code execution
summary:
Affected: npm: signalk-server, npm: @signalk/resources-provider ### Summary Path traversal in the Signal K resources and applicationData APIs lets an
unauthenticated or low-privileged user read, write and delete files outside
the storage root. Reading <config>/security.json discloses the JWT signing
secret, enabling admin token forgery and remote code execution. ### Details ## Description The v2 REST resources API `GET /signalk/v2/api/resources/:resourceType/:resourceId` passes `resourceId` to `FileStore.getResource()` without validation. `getResource()` builds the file path with `path.join(this.resources[type].path, itemUuid)` followed by `readFile` + `JSON.parse`, so a `%2F`-encoded multi-level traversal (`..%2F..%2F..%2F..%2F`) escapes the resource storage directory and returns any JSON file on the server (source: `src/api/resources/index.ts:559-600`, `packages/resources-provider-plugin/src/filestorage.ts:115-125`). Because the JWT signing secret is stored in plaintext in `<config>/security.json` (generated at `src/tokensecurity.ts:271`, persisted via `saveSecurityConfig` at `src/security.ts:377`), an unauthenticated attacker on deployments with `allow_readonly=true` (a supported, UI-toggleable configuration granting anonymous read access) can: 1. **Read `<config>/security.json`** — disclosing the JWT signing secret (512-hex) and user password hashes.
